_readme: Respellings applied to the text the voice model SPEAKS. Captions and on-screen
text are untouched, so the viewer always sees correct spelling.
Add an entry whenever a word comes out unclear. Fixed once, fixed everywhere.
A leading comma buys the word breathing room; a dense word swallows consonants.

"3 \u2014" -> "then": ten seeds and five respellings were measured and the model never produces an English dental fricative in this voice — frication came out 7.5-25ms where /th/ needs 45-160, and the two spellings that did change the sound broke the word into "The Re". So the number leaves the audio and stays in the caption, which is exactly what this file is for.

The "3" mapping was removed on his instruction: he wants the number SPOKEN, not only written. Ten seeds and five spellings never produced the fricative, so the remaining untried levers are exaggeration, cfg_weight, temperature and the carrier phrase around the word — being swept now rather than declared impossible.

23.8, continued: swept exaggeration (0.35/0.50/0.65), cfg_weight (0.15/0.30), and temperature (0.75/0.90/0.95) — 6 combinations plus the two lines that already say the word in reel-01 (line 7, 'three seeds') and reel-02 (line 6, 'Same three steps'), across three full builds and one dedicated sweep. Every single measured take came back burst or absent by audio/burst.py; not one hit frication. That is roughly 20 independent draws total (this session's 6-combo sweep plus in-build retries) all landing the same way, against a genuinely different carrier sentence in reel-02 — so this is not a fluke of one script or one seed range, it is this voice consistently failing to produce the fricative regardless of the lever pulled. Also confirmed why the OLDER duration-based check (audio/th_check.py) never flagged this: it explicitly refuses to judge a word that opens an utterance (no preceding closure to compare against — see its ONSET_GAP_DB guard), which is exactly where 'three' sits in both scripts. audio/burst.py's own calibration set was measured mid-sentence ('in three seconds'), not utterance-initial, so even its verdict here is measuring something it was not directly validated for. Bottom line: further seed/param rerolling is very unlikely to find a clean take from data alone. The open paths are (a) his ear picks the least-bad of the candidates already generated (see SUNDAY.md), (b) a carrier phrase that does not put 'three' at the very start of an utterance, or (c) revisit whether the number needs to be spoken at all, now with far more evidence behind that question than the original ten-seed sweep had.

notes.bottom: He flagged reel-05's "the platform hides the bottom on purpose" as sounding British — a mid-word flapped T that script_lint.py's flapped-T regex doesn't catch (it only matches word-final -er/-le/-ing/-ed, not a T in the middle like bot-tom). Verified with line_doctor.py: "boddom" measured -24.4dB tail energy vs -32.5dB unrespelled, and Whisper found the word fine (unlike "our" below) — a real, validated fix, not a guess.
notes.Personalization: Six syllables landed in 0.86s and the L disappeared. British spelling scores higher and the comma slows it to 5 syllables/sec.
notes.our: He flagged reel-07's outro ("in our bio") as sounding British — same class as harder/first, a swallowed final R. Tried respelling it ("ourr", then "are") the way harder/first were fixed, but both broke line_doctor.py's own Whisper-based word lookup (reported the target word MISSING), so neither could be measured or validated, and the unvalidated "ourr" that got committed anyway did not actually fix the sound he heard. Removed the respelling entirely and instead cut the word from reel-07's line ("tap the bio link" instead of "tap the link in our bio") — the same move already used for "wrong" and "not sure" this session: when a word won't respell cleanly, reword around it rather than keep guessing at spellings. reel-05 still says "our own videos" mid-sentence (not utterance-final, different R context) and is queued for a full rebuild — check that line by ear when it's rebuilt rather than assuming this same defect is there.
